text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- B.C. gets behind tobacco suits: Law would enable province, residents to team up against manufacturers for health costs.
- Court backs Israeli PM: Troubles mount in other areas.
- Native land claim 'giant' awakens: Supreme Court hears case today.
- Hong Kong a homecoming queen: From the smallest village to the major cities, China is getting ready to blow the lid off celebrating the return of the prodigal territory.
- Despite award, ruined businessman's ordeal drags on: At long last, payment of nearly C$9 million has been ordered to man who lost everything because he wasn't told everything, but new hurdles loom.
- G7 summit seen as 'pageant': Analysts expect Clinton to shine spotlight on Russia and ignore tough global issues.
- Information giants do battle: The big financial data providers, Dow Jones, Reuters and Bloomberg, face a huge technological change as the Internet shifts the landscape.
- Ukraine stymies foreign investors: Canadian firms battle bureaucracy.
- Internet stocks play a Snakes and Ladders game.
- The bulls keep running: North American markets appear to be unstoppable as interest rates stay low, bond yields fall and both the TSE and Dow roar to record highs.
- Another big miner moving to Toronto.
